chapter: Trent's band: touring, sidemen and breakup
title: John Fielding the singer, from Hot Springs
summary: Fielding sang ballads but played no instrument, died in Pensacola, and later managed Trent's small band.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Now, Fielding opened the Adolphus with you?
Right.
Where was Fielding from, Little Rock?
Hot Springs.
Now that has to be unusual because wasn't Fielding already working with you guys when you were working in Arkansas, before you came to Texas?
Yes, but you know, John Fielding was with the great Sterling Todd--
Oh, with the Road City Orchestra.
The Road City Orchestra.
But Fielding never played an instrument, did he?
No, never played an instrument, but he was a wonderful singer, a beautiful guy and dressed beautifully.
He wasn't in front of
the band, directing it, was he?
No, he couldn't direct anything.
He just got up and sang?
Just sang.
He had to be the first guy to sing with a black band I would think.
That's right.
He had to be.
He was not a swing singer; he was a ballad singer?
Mostly ballads.
And you say he died in Florida?
I think it was Pensacola, Florida.
What, about two years ago?
No, it was longer than that.
He's been dead now for maybe nine--
Did he leave any family?
Yes, his family is in Hot Springs now, his sister.

He's the one who used to say, I got to find John Fielding, John Fielding has the scrapbook of the band, because John Fielding became his manager later on in the thirties, after the band broke up and he started the small band. He had the small band with Charlie Christian in 1937, '38, and John Fielding was his manager at that time.
